newsitem.title: USA: GCA Nov. coffee stock data seen slightly bearish.
newsitem.headline: GCA Nov. coffee stock data seen slightly bearish.

text.p: U.S. coffee futures are likely to ease a bit after monthly inventory data released late Monday showed a slight increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks, traders and analysts said.
Supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses rose in November by 4,000 60-kg bags, to 1,264,000 bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported.
"It is not a surprise. We are not talking a lot of coffee here," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "But we may see some pressure and a general erosion in prices over time."
The port of Houston, Texas, posted the largest gain in coffee stocks. Houston stocks rose by 44,000 bags to 123,000 bags, the GCA said.
Inventories increased by 17,000 bags, to 104,000 bags in Laredo, Texas. Warehouse stocks in New Orleans also increased in November, rising 8,000 bags to 529,000 bags.
In New York, however, inventories decreased by 16,000 bags, to 152,000 bags.

But while many analysts said the build in stocks, the first since March, was to be expected with many Latin American countries' coffee harvests well underway, some traders had expected a further decline in consumer coffee inventories during November.

"It should not be a surprise with more coffee coming in from Central America and Colombia," one analyst said. "Although some people felt the drawdown would continue going into the high consumption period."
Increasing the risk of a sell-off, traders said, was the report Monday of a substantial gain in weekly U.S. certified stocks.
The CSCE report showed exchange-certified coffee stocks in the U.S. warehouses rose by 10,250 60-kg bags in the week ended December 13, to 12,571 bags.
In addition, 11,000 bags of coffee were certified for delivery at Miami through December 16, after the close of the weekly reporting period, bringing the total certified inventory to 23,571 bags.
While neither of the figures was especially negative on its own, traders said their release on the same day created a potential double-whammy for prices.
"The certifieds went up too, and that may cause a little more pressure," the trader said.
The CSCE reported an additional 9,000 bags were pending grading.
